ctx.x: after a few days of hard rehearsing we had a nice repertoire and we also had some head arrangements. We incorporated the band and took the name of Harlem Rythm Makers. Jazz had not been very popular or well known in Egypt until Willie went there and his band made a big hit.

So when we returned with a less commercial band than Willie had, we made a big hit with the clientele of the Monseigneur. Many of the young jazz lovers, who were mostly from rich families, came to hear us at least three times a week. There were many rich Greek families in Egypt and also many rich young Egyptians whom we became well acquainted with. We wore a grey suit uniform for the afternoon matinees and tuxedos at night. Every night the band got better and I became the featured singer. My voice was not great but I had more nerve to try and sing a song than the rest of the fellows. One night we were singing like mad on a number and when I finished my two choruses, I finished on a high note and Arthur Pay (who was an amateur drummer) stopped right after I took my horn from my chops.
